title: Google Play now lets anyone build private, vibe-coded apps that run on Android
key_facts: Google announced on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 that people can launch their own vibe-coded apps on their Android phone through Google Play with a standard Google account, without publishing them publicly (TechCrunch).
These personal apps do not appear in Play search or listings and are shared with no one but their creator.
Users can build an app with Google AI Studio and then launch it for their own use; the apps must still comply with Google Play policies.
At first the feature is available to users in the US aged 18 and up.
In the coming months users will be able to share their creations with a network of trusted friends, and a popular personal app could later move to the public store after trust and safety reviews.

Google Play also adds a Game Finder recommendation engine (US, English), Community Posts, 48-hour "Sprints" challenges and comparisons in its Ask Play assistant, with Play apps more deeply integrated in Gemini.
Google Play is adding support for an age-range feature that lets parents share a child's age range, not the exact birthdate, with developers.
quote_evidence: These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator.
Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up.
In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends.
why_it_matters_hint: Ordinary people can now run apps they made with AI on their own Android phones without going through public release.
